chunks: Till whatever is written as ordained approaches its end, the affairs complete their destined limits, the posteriors join the anteriors and whatever Allāh wills takes place in the shape of resurrection of His creation.
Then He would convulse the sky and split it. He would quake the earth and shake it. He would root out the mountains and scatter them.
They would crush each other out of awe of His Glory and fear of His Dignity.
He would take out everyone who is in it. He would refresh them after they had been worn out and collect them after they had been separated.
Then He would set them apart for questioning about the hidden deeds and secret acts.
He would then divide them into two groups, rewarding one and punishing the other.
ai.seo_question: What happens to the cosmos and humanity on the Day of Judgement according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This passage from Nahj al-Balagha vividly depicts the cosmic dissolution and renewal (tajdid) of creation, emphasizing Allah's absolute power to upend the physical universe as a prelude to the final accounting. It highlights the theological concept of distinguishing between the apparent and hidden aspects of human deeds, leading to the bifurcation of humanity into the blessed and the wretched, a theme central to Shia eschatological reflections on divine justice.
